name: soft-key-goal
task: Grab the key, and after that get to the goal square if you can.

value.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: the clauses match the task exactly. 'Grab the key' is an unconditional command, so hard Existence(has_key) is right; it is not redundant because the hard Precedence alone forces nothing and the goal step is only soft. 'and after that' states the order, and the preference cue 'if you can' covers only the step it qualifies, so hard Precedence(has_key, at_goal) with the order staying hard is correct. 'get to the goal square if you can' is a preference, so soft Existence(at_goal) is right. No clause is added (the door is never mentioned in the task and the environment already guarantees the door ordering), and every hard requirement of the task is captured.

texts: The agent must acquire the yellow key at some point.
The goal square must not be reached before the key has been acquired.
The agent should reach the goal square, if possible.
